data.name: Eliab
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Eliab means 'My God is God'. In the Bible, Eliab is the third oldest brother of David and a captain in Saul's army. He is a valiant warrior, and when David decides to go to the battlefront to bring back the ephod, Eliab attempts to stop him.
data.numerology_meaning: A loving, nurturing, and compassionate being

in_hebrew.name: אליעב
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא אביי, האל הוא אבי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליעב הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא אביי' או 'האל הוא אבי'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'אל' שפירושו אלוהים, ו'יעב' שפירושו אב. השם אליעב מופיע בתנ'ך ככינויו של אחד מבני ישראל, וגם ככינויו של אחד מהשרים של מחנה ישראל.

in_greek.name: Ελιάβ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο πατέρας μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ελιάβ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος אליעב, που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο πατέρας μου'. Στην ελληνική Βίβλο, το όνομα Ελιάβ αναφέρεται σε δύο πρόσωπα, ένα από τα οποία ήταν αρχηγός της φυλής Γαδ και το άλλο ήταν πατέρας του Νεμάν.

in_latin.name: Eliab
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eliab derivatur ex hebraeo nomine אליעב, quod significat 'Deus est pater meus'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Eliab fuit usitatum inter credentes christianos, qui inspirationem ex scripturis sacris et traditione christiana trahebant.

in_english.name: Eliab
in_english.meaning: God is my father or My God is the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eliab originates from the Hebrew name אליעב (Eliab), meaning 'My God is the Lord' or 'God is my father'. It is composed of two Hebrew words: 'El' (אל), meaning God, and 'Ab' (אב), meaning father. In the Bible, Eliab appears as the name of several individuals, including a leader of the tribe of Gad and the father of one of King David's brothers. The name holds significant spiritual meaning, reflecting a deep connection with God as a paternal figure. Throughout Christian tradition, Eliab has been adopted as a given name, symbolizing faith, divine guidance, and paternal love.

biblical_reference.note: Eliab was the name of several individuals in the Hebrew Bible, including a son of Abinadab and a brother of David.

data.cultural_impact: Eliab is a name with deep historical roots as it is mentioned in the Old Testament of the Bible. The name carries a strong military connotation, given Eliab's role as a captain in Saul's army. Additionally, in Jewish literature, Eliab is considered a type of Messiah figure, representing strength, valor, and divine leadership.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Eliab means 'My God is God,' reflecting a profound faith in the one true deity. It reminds us of the importance of recognizing God's sovereignty in our lives and trusting in His divine plan, even when facing challenges or oppositions. Eliab's courage and unwavering loyalty to Saul demonstrate that our faith in God should not waver, even when we encounter difficult circumstances or adversaries.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Eliab is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Jeduthun. The name Eliab carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Eliab is a biblical figure mentioned in the Old Testament as a Levite and the father of Jeduthun, a musician in King David's court.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

It is a reminder that God is not just an abstract deity, but a personal God who is always present and faithful. This name inspires an unwavering trust in the divine, instilling a sense of strength and security in the face of adversity.
